text:
sam: Thinking we should converge on a smaller coalescer interface + explicit backpressure tactics. The current surface is too permissive and it's leading to subtle memory spikes and long-tail latency.

sam: Proposal sketch: a tiny interface that only exposes enqueue(), try_coalesce(deadline_ns), and on_backpressure(signal). Keep KV warmup orthogonal but provide hooks so coalescer can indicate when batches will trigger warmup.

nisha: Can you expand on "hooks"? are you imagining a callback or a heartbeat metric?

sam: callback from coalescer to kvcache manager like `on_warmup_candidate(batch_id, hint)` — cheap, best-effort. No blocking. 

leo: I worry about coupling. If coalescer starts hinting too early we can waste memory warming large KV ranges. Maybe hints should carry a cost estimate and TTL.

marisol: Also +1 to keeping the interface tiny. Operationally we want easy knobs: a soft-credit budget and a hard-evict threshold. Defaults should be conservative.

leo: Example soft-credit flow: coalescer holds N credits, try_coalesce reduces credits by estimated_tokens, background refill based on observed throughput. If credits exhausted => on_backpressure("soft").

tj: Long-tail scenario: small requests get batched into one big batch because coalescer waited for credits; that big batch stalls other tenants. How do we avoid head-of-line blocking?

sam: Two levers: (1) deadline-aware coalescing (deadline wins over fullness) and (2) preemptible micro-batches that can be split if they exceed a per-tenant token cap at execution time.

nisha: Splitting at execution time adds complexity but seems doable. We'll need determinism for tracing; idempotent replays are a must.

marisol: From rollout POV, we should be able to flip between: immediate-ack fastpath, coalesce-with-hints, and strict-queue slowpath. Each mode has different cost/latency tradeoffs.

infra-bot: incident 2026-02-14T09:12Z - observed ephemeral OOM on gpu-node-7 during a warmup storm, correlated with aggressive coalescing.

sam: Exactly why tighter controls matter. The OOM pattern is: many warmup hints + prefetch + large coalesced batch. We need an escape hatch: bounded warmup budget per-node and per-tenant.

leo: Telemetry we need for the experiment: batch_size_histogram (by tenant), coalesce_wait_ms, warmup_candidates/sec, warmup_memory_bytes, preempt_splits_count, ack_mode.

marisol: Also add rollout guard: automated rollback if p50 latency increases > 10% or memory > 70% of node capacity for 5m.

sam: Minimal proto interface I can sketch this week. Pseudo: 

```
interface SlimCoalescer {
  Enqueue(req_id, tokens, tenant_id, deadline_ns)
  TryCoalesce(now_ns) -> Optional<Batch>
  OnBackpressure(level:"soft"|"hard", reason:string)
  // hooks
  EmitWarmupHint(batch_id, estimated_kv_keys, cost_estimate_bytes)
}
```

sam: TryCoalesce returns quickly; implementers must avoid blocking syscalls. Splits happen at execution layer when `batch.tokens > token_cap(tenant)` and are recorded as preempt_splits_count.

nisha: I'm happy to own a small experiment: implement SlimCoalescer shim, enable hints as opt-in on a single dedicated pod pool, and collect the telemetry Leo listed.

leo: I'll add the Prom rules and dashboards (bucketed histograms). Also write a small load test that exercises warmup-heavy traces.

marisol: I'll own rollout plan + alerting thresholds. Suggest starting on staging with 5% traffic and a 30m soak.

tj: One more thought: backpressure signals should be directly actionable by frontends (e.g., reduce prefetch depth, switch to immediate-ack). We need a tiny signal protocol for clients.

sam: Agree. Lightweight proto: {level, suggested_prefetch, suggested_mode, ttl_ms}. Keep default TTL short (1s) to prevent stale hints.

marisol: OK — volunteers: nisha (impl), leo (telemetry), marisol (rollout), sam (design + implementation help), tj (client signal integration). I'll schedule a 45m sync tomorrow.

sam: Thanks. I'll drop the initial PR with shim + unit tests and a runbook link. :thumbsup:

nisha: Great, will start on the shim. Quick Q: do we want to log warmup hints at DEBUG only?

sam: DEBUG for bulk hint details, INFO for hint counts and aggregated memory estimate.

leo: Putting observability checklist in the issue now.
